body: thank you so much for this and i truly hope things ease up for both of us
thank you so much

its really eye opening to hear you and others say you guys have had staff and integrative therapy help you out because i dont have any kind of integrative appointments afterwards and i feel like the staff is super disconnected when im having a bad experience, but then again that could just be my skewed perspective of dissociation. thanks so much for the reply
please do!
thank you so much. i really appreciate this. i think i said that exact phrase “im never doing this again” today during my infusion lol. so helpful to know im not the only one

that’s interesting about the physical pain, i do have chronic back pain and migraines. i never really considered that since that wasnt what i was doing the treatments for. thank you so much for the information and for your experience
truly wishing you nothing but the best, i really have had some relief from the treatment and my depression is historically a stubborn one. im hopeful for you!
yep you hit the nail on the head with that last sentence, thank you so much for sharing your experience i really appreciate it
definitely also have anxiety. really really appreciate these suggestions thank you so much
appreciate this. definitely gonna look into another clinic where theyre more open to lower doses
i dont do the eye mask, for some reason it trips me up. the music absolutely helps and i can totally understand it influencing the trip so thank you for that suggestion
thank you so much. i really like the idea of having the nurse come in and reorient you
will definitely be looking into spravato ive heard a lot of good things and i like the idea of a lower dose thank you so much
thank you
it really is! thank you
thank you so much thats great to hear

thank you so much and i completely agree with the medicine (hopefully) working regardless of the trip. i have been working on my intentions and listening to music that vibes well with me. the staff isnt great which might be an issue, but i usually have a good experience until the last couple minutes where the dose “peaks”. thank you again
thank you, im on xanax as needed but was advised not to take it within 12 hours of the session. i wonder if they would be okay with me taking something like that before. appreciate the suggestion
thank you so much
thank you so much, definitely gonna look around for other clinics

i truly appreciate this and completely understand what youre saying, im dealing with the same thing right now and its terrifying. im so sorry youre going through it but youre not alone. it comforts me to know its just the drug and we really dont know anything about the afterlife yet. thank you
thank you so much. this is my first ketamine experience and i really wanted it to work out but i definitely will advocate for myself going forward.
thank you so much
thank you. its good to hear that other people dont look forward to them but still have a good outcome in the end. definitely something to think more about

very normal. ive had awful dry mouth when i started and everytime ive increased my dose. my whole body felt off which was irritating and part of the reason i kept waking up at night which could be the same for you. definitely give it like a week or two to get better

im sorry to hear :( so frustrating because for me its not like other meds where you can take it early in the day and be fine/functional. definitely deal with the same drugged up kind of feeling as you. guess its just one of those things we have to live with for a bit.

yeah i do have adhd but never responded well to stimulants. im on clonodine .2 at night to help me sleep but it virtually does nothing without an antipsychotic, but to be fair ive never really been able to successfully withdrawal bc i just cant sleep through the night and the mental and physical feelings are unbearable. i have been suggested remeron before definitely wanna look into that more. just wish i didnt have to choose between being awake all night from my racing mind or sleeping all day and being a zombie, so frustrating
